advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the G6/E4/T3 COHORT membership test with the corpus E5 reads (code_review_adjudication.jsonl carries dimension names, not cohort labels) so AC3 is a real check, not a tautology.
evidence: Contrast: the sibling E6 harness reads a DIFFERENT corpus where the labels live — adjudication_corpus.jsonl:1 `"criterion": "G6", "criteria": ["G6"]`, matched via `r.get("criterion") in COHORT` (e6_judge_reliability.py:109)
e5 lines 103-108: `acc = "na"` then `if in_cohort: cohort_members += 1` then `if acc != "na": non_na += 1` — acc is never reassigned, so the `non_na` branch is dead
summary field `"asserted_capability_confirmed_na_for_all": non_na == 0` (line 152 region) is thus always True
main() gate: `ok = summary["byte_identical"] and summary["asserted_capability_confirmed_na_for_all"]` (line 166) — the second conjunct is a constant
advisory.finding: The G6/E4/T3 cohort membership test is inert on this corpus: `criteria & COHORT` (COHORT={"G6","E4","T3"}) is matched against code_review_adjudication.jsonl, whose `criteria` are dimension names (e.g. ["correctness","scope-intent","regression"]) and whose `criterion` is a comma-joined dimension string — never a cohort label. So `in_cohort` is structurally always False and `cohort_members` is always 0 regardless of the data, making the AC3 '0 findings in the cohort' result a tautology rather than a verified check.
merged_from: `asserted_capability_confirmed_na_for_all` is a constant-True flag, not a computed result. `acc = "na"` is hardcoded unconditionally at line 104; the `if in_cohort:` branch only increments a counter and never sets acc to a non-na value, so `non_na` can never be > 0 and `non_na == 0` is always True. main()'s PASS/FAIL gate ANDs byte_identical with this always-true flag, so the flag contributes nothing to the gate verdict.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Either assert a bound on max_validity_reconstruction_error in the PASS gate or soften the docstring claim that the artifact serves as a corpus consistency check.
evidence: e5 lines 62-70 docstring: 'a faithful reconstruction lets the artifact double as an internal-consistency check on the corpus (recorded validity ≈ reconstructed validity)'
e5 line 121: `max_recon_err = max(max_recon_err, abs(pre["validity"] - validity))` — only accumulated, never asserted
main() gate (line 166) checks only byte_identical + the always-true na flag — max_recon_err is not in the PASS predicate
advisory.finding: `max_validity_reconstruction_error` is recorded (0.0556 in the artifact) but never bounded or asserted, while the `_binary_for_validity` docstring claims the artifact 'doubles as an internal-consistency check on the corpus (recorded validity ≈ reconstructed validity)'. Because reconstruction quantizes to k/n over the 9-question PRE set, recorded validities off the k/9 grid produce a nonzero error that passes silently — the claimed consistency check is not enforced.
